one_liner: Exact-integer QuickHull for convex hulls in any dimension, inside DGtal; authors claim over 2x faster than CGAL convex_hull_3.
what_it_does: DGtal::QuickHull<Kernel> computes the convex hull of lattice (integer) points, or of rational approximations of real points, in any dimension of 2 or more. With a Delaunay kernel it also computes the Delaunay cell complex by lifting to one dimension higher. You call setInput(points, remove_duplicates = true), then computeConvexHull(), then read the vertices with getVertexPositions() and the oriented facet vertex lists with getFacetVertices(), plus index maps between input, de-duplicated and vertex numbering. ConvexityHelper wraps it in one-call helpers that return lattice polytopes, SurfaceMesh/PolygonalSurface boundaries or cell complexes, and GenericLatticeConvexHull (DGtal 2.1) handles inputs that are not full-dimensional. The interface is unrelated to CGAL's convex_hull_3, and its output facets are polygons, not triangles.
how_it_is_fast: It implements Barber et al.'s Quickhull (1996): start from a full-dimensional simplex, assign each point to one facet it lies above, repeatedly take the furthest point of a facet, find visible facets through neighbour links, build the horizon ridges, cone new facets to the point, merge coplanar facets and reassign the outside points. Geometry is delegated to a kernel that uses exact integer arithmetic (int64 by default, optional BigInteger) for facet normals, intercepts and above/on tests, so there is no floating-point filtering or exact-arithmetic fallback cost. Coplanar facets are merged instead of triangulated, which keeps the facet count low on lattice inputs where coplanarity is common.
when_to_use: 3D convex hulls of integer or voxel/lattice point sets (digital geometry, voxelized shapes) where you want exact, robust results without CGAL's licence or kernel machinery
Hulls in 4D-6D or higher of lattice points, which convex_hull_3 does not cover; the docs give the int64 coordinate limits per dimension (about 1.5e6 in 3D, 4e4 in 4D, 5e3 in 5D, 1.2e3 in 6D)

Floating-point points that may be snapped to a rational grid: the rational kernel rounds x * precision to integers, and the docs report 1e7 points in a radius-1000 ball (precision 1024) in about 7.9 s total on a 2.7 GHz quad-core i7 MacBook Pro
You need polygonal (merged coplanar) facets, for example lattice polytopes or H-representations, rather than a triangulated hull
Projects already using DGtal for digital topology or geometry, where the hull comes at no extra dependency cost
when_not_to_use: Delaunay triangulation: the same docs say the lifted-hull Delaunay is 5-10x slower than CGAL's point-location method (1M lattice points in 2D took about 20.7 s), so use CGAL, Delaunay32 or gDel3D/HXT instead
Incremental or dynamic hulls with point insertion and removal: the docs say it is not tailored for that

Large coordinates or high dimensions with default int64: overflow is possible past the documented bounds, is reported only as an InvalidRidge or InvalidConvexHull status, and switching to BigInteger costs about 25x (35x when both coordinate and internal types are BigInteger)
When you need a measured speedup: the '2x faster than CGAL' line has no published CGAL timings, point distributions, compiler or benchmark program
Small dependency footprint or permissive licence: it ships inside the LGPL-3.0 DGtal library, which needs C++20, CMake 3.20, Boost headers, zlib and Eigen

integration.dependencies: DGtal headers (DGtal 2.x is 'almost header only'), Boost headers (fetched via CPM at CMake time), zlib and Eigen as required DGtal build dependencies; the QuickHull core itself uses only DGtal kernel types and the standard library
integration.min_toolchain: C++20 compiler, CMake 3.20 (DGtal 2.0+); Visual Studio supported per README
integration.platforms: any (portable C++, no SIMD); CI covers Linux, macOS and Windows; Python wheels are published to PyPI, though whether QuickHull is exposed there is not documented
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the implementation is single-threaded and the QuickHull object holds mutable state, so use one instance per thread

gotchas: Facets are not simplicial: a facet can be any planar polygon (or higher-dimensional cell), so code expecting CGAL's triangle mesh must triangulate the facets itself

Roughly half of total time goes to duplicate removal (a sort over the input, 4.2 s of 7.9 s for 1e7 points); pass remove_duplicates = false to setInput only if your input is known to be duplicate-free
Choose CoordinateInteger and InternalInteger to fit your coordinate range and dimension; overflow is not an exception but a bad status (InvalidRidge or InvalidConvexHull) that you must check
The rational kernels round coordinates to multiples of 1/precision, so distinct real points can collapse into one vertex, and too large a precision overflows int64
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No sibling entry is a dedicated 3D convex hull: pgl beats CGAL on convex_hull_2 in the plane only, and gDel3D or HXT target 3D Delaunay, where DGtal's lifted method is 5-10x slower than CGAL. Pick DGtal QuickHull for exact integer hulls in 3D or more dimensions, especially if you already use DGtal; pick Delaunay32, gDel3D or HXT for triangulations.
verified_claims_summary: The only comparison is one sentence repeated in QuickHull.h and the module docs: 'generally more than twice faster than CGAL convex_hull_3' for the Cartesian and EPICK kernels, with no CGAL numbers, point sets, CGAL version, compiler or hardware given, and no CGAL benchmark in the repository. The docs' own DGtal-only timings (MacBook Pro, 2.7 GHz quad-core Intel Core i7) are 7.9 s total for 1e7 random lattice points in a radius-1000 ball, of which 3.2 s is the Quickhull core and 4.2 s is duplicate removal.
status_note: Actively maintained (DGtal 2.1 released and 2.1.1 in development, last commit 2026-09-23, 398 stars, SGP 2016 Software Award), LGPL-3.0, with QuickHull present since DGtal 1.2; there are no QuickHull-specific issues, but you must take the whole DGtal library to use it.
